rationale: The sign logic is correct (NEG(invch) is the inventory build, apalch the payable financing), but this is essentially the archive's "Supplier-Unfunded Inventory Investment" numerator re-scaled by the archive's "Working-Capital Diversion Share" capex-share denominator — a recombination of two already-tested constructs on the same sparse cash-flow items rather than a new mechanism.

Subtracting three years of *total* D&A (dpc covers tangible depreciation too) from three-year intangible growth is dimensionally mismatched, so the signal will be dominated by cumulative depreciation intensity rather than intangible capitalization — the hypothesis does not match what the expression computes, and it is otherwise just a horizon extension of the existing Net Intangible Capitalization signal.

Internally consistent (NEG(recch) is receivable accumulation, sstk share is nonnegative, product sign matches the negative prediction) and it substitutes a targeted earnings-management component for the aggregate accrual in the prior issuance-share signal, though it remains an incremental variant within an already crowded issuance×accrual family.

The construction is coherent and the maintenance-investment conditioner is continuous rather than sparse, but it is yet another accrual×conditioner multiplicative variant and its direction directly contradicts the archive's "Underdepreciated Accrual Expansion" (which conditioned on *low* depreciation intensity for the same expected sign), a tension the reasoning never confronts.

A genuinely novel accounting-reconciliation/data-integrity construct that is correctly specified given invch's decrease-minus-increase convention, though the absolute-value framing gives it no directional economics (M&A-driven inventory additions and divestitures load identically) and it will inherit the sparse cash-flow-item coverage.

A clean, internally consistent tangible-asset reconciliation residual with broad coverage that isolates PPE growth not attributable to reported capex net of depreciation — distinct from the archive's asset-level residual and not a direct restatement of the standard asset-growth or investment anomalies, with the caveat that it will partly proxy for acquisitiveness.
